boat.full_description:
Eagle Owl is a Cornish Shrimper. She has an inboard Yanmar 1GM10 diesel engine. GRP hull and wooden Spars. Her rig is technically gunter rig as the gaff can be hauled to lie parallel to the mast when not reefed. She has two berths and a galley. She is equipped with Garmin plotter, NMEA network with ships WIFI, ships radio, AIS transceiver. She has solar power.  

She was ordered from Cornish Crabbers as a new build at the London Boat show by Gary Pearlman in Jan 1987 and delivered June 1987.

The Pearlman's lived in Chalfont, Buckinghamshire at the time. She was named Garatania of Chalfont. Garatania was an anagram of family names together. Gary Pearlman was a keen sailor and had a holiday home in Salcombe so would often sail her there. Then she was moored in Topsham on the river Exe. Sadly Gary Pearlman died in 1999 aged only 46.

From July 1999 she was owned and sailed by Robin Gibbon & Hew Naylor. She sailed at Tollesbury and in the Essex Estuary. She was renamed Emily Anne. Her first mooring was on the Stour at Manningtree. Emily Anne took part in the 2000 East Coast Rally followed by rallies in Holland and the Solent together with a number of regattas at such places as Aldeburgh, Waldringfield and Felixstowe Ferry.

Robin was an ex-professional Ship's Master with a huge experience of sailing in a large variety of yachts of all sizes. With his experience, he became Emily Anne's extremely successful skipper while Hew Naylor crewed. Emily Anne raced regularly and was always either first or second to Robin Whittle in Bumble Chugger (#124) which is an outboard Shrimper and was fierce competition. By 2014 Robin and Hew were no longer fit enough to sail and put her up for sale.  

In 2016 she was Bought by Nigel Emmett and moved to North Norfolk. He had previously owned and sailed a much newer Shrimper and hoped to do so again. However she wasn't sailed during this period. She needed considerable maintenance and restoration by then and after having her engine was rebuilt by Archer Engineering at considerable expense, was kept on the hard at Morston Near Blakeney. The following year when it become apparent that the work needed was more than could be accommodated she was put up for sale again.  

In August 2017 she was bought by Ann Ingham her current owner and towed from Norfolk to Lancashire. Later that year she underwent repairs at Cornish Crabbers which included cockpit sole, centre plate casing, shroud plates, and rudder hangings. She was then berthed and sailed in Preston Dock to test her seaworthiness and following that on Consiston. In 2019 further restoration and improvements were carried out including fitting VHF radio and arial, AIS transceiver, dual batteries, new masthead lights, solar panel charging with VSR, Garmin plotter, auto bilge pump. And repainting the cabin. She was sailed in Plymouth where she was renamed Eagle Owl in a renaming ceremony on the water in Plymouth Harbour accompanied by fellow SOA members. Then she sailed on Derwentwater, and came to be berthed in her current home port of Lytham at Ribble Cruising Club.  
In 2020 further modifications, repairs and maintenance were carried out including sanding to bare wood and Cetol to gaff and boom, new running rigging, new stove, re-galvanising the centre plate, stainless replacement fairleads, depth sounder fitted, cutlass bearing replaced, stuffing box renewed, engine serviced and new bunk cushions. She continued to sail in the Lytham Estuary when regulations allowed.  

In 2021 further work entailed sanding and cetol to mast, rudder repair where mahogany had split, the hull under the water line was stripped and repainted with antifoul, sails repaired, pivoting bowsprit modification was installed, new Stainless steel fittings, and mast tabernacle blasted and powder coated. And she sailed at Lytham and attended SOA ISW Suffolk Rivers based at Suffolk Yacht Harbour on the River Orwell.  

In 2022 in addition to regular sailing at her home port she attended the SOA Shrimper week at Largs. She also took part in the Ribble Cruising club Xmas Cruise in December, which was a short lived expedition as the was a hailstorm.  

2023 saw Eagle Owl participate in the OGA60 party returning to Suffolk yacht harbour where tumultuous downpours over 5 days were not enough to dampen spirits. The OGA60 event for small boats on Ullswater in August had much better weather and Eagle Owl sailed the length of the lake. December saw Eagle Owl taking part in the xmas cruise in pleasant conditions crewed by pirates!  

2024 Eagle Owl joined Shrimper week in Falmouth and sailed the LaLa rally through the Menai Straights from Conwy to Caernafon and back. In addition joined many activities in the Lytham estuary. 2025 saw Eagle Owl in Milford Haven and again on Ullswater. In 2026 Eagle Owl once again returned to Plymouth.  

Eagle Owl is based at her home port at Lytham, although being a trailer sailor also resides at home out of season. Her crew comprises Bell and Brodie, two cockapoos, who can be seen in numerous photos. Human crew are always welcome.  
2027 will be her 50th anniversary.
boat.name: Eagle Owl
